# Decisive older-source repairs: three frozen interfaces

Read status is separate from correctness. Repository commit687dfc0640ee80654bcbdbe38cb13d6e1f1586ce is unchanged. The original-source summaries below were independently checked at the stated scope, not copied as proof validation from the repository.

## Positive-characteristic group rings

Formanek1973 primary PDF acquired, sha256195f1f5f5bb9208d43e63ba0b086b4a325645b9d0097cf61cf8bba1b57f63f9b. Read p366 / PDF1, Theorems1–3; text lines9–25. The no-idempotent theorem there assumes a torsion-free Noetherian group and characteristic0. Arbitrary-characteristic Theorem3 restricts trace to the prime subfield. URL: https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/25AF425E2069C808258EA860D2329372/S0008414X00050392a.pdf/idempotents-in-noetherian-group-rings.pdf

Burger-Valette1998 primary scanned PDF acquired, sha2564a80e0000b8b42fac420818dd96cb5b51472abc9e93fe62919a7031775d8cc5e. PDF8 rendered at150dpi and viewed in full. Lemma4.1 assumes characteristic p, no p-torsion and no relevant power-conjugacy, and concludes tau(e)=0 or1. Proposition4.2 concerns the complex group algebra, using characteristic0 trace positivity after reduction modulo primes. The original page does not convert the characteristic-p trace restriction into triviality of e. URL: https://people.math.ethz.ch/~burger/pub/1998_Idempotents.pdf

BLR2008 published Journal of Topology PDF acquired from academic mirror, sha2565028632393a6680a169fed740a75f28d0d2bd8f928512dcf01a81f3306ab0140. Read printedpp62–63 / PDF6–7, Theorem1.12 and cited paragraph; text lines250–316. The paper still prints the stronger all-field hyperbolic claim and attributes it to the sources above. Its separate K0 theorem adds stable finiteness, characteristic0 or soficity. This establishes a scope discrepancy in the printed attribution, not the truth or falsity of the stronger claim. URL: https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/blr2.pdf ; publication DOI https://doi.org/10.1112/jtopol/jtm008

Independent elementary obstruction to the old no-go inference: in any unital ring with ab=1 and ba!=1, r=1-ba is a nonzero idempotent because (ba)^2=b(ab)a=ba. # Integration criteria, frozen before field results

Time: 2026-10-08; programme source is DATA. Pinned repository commit: 687dfc0640ee80654bcbdbe38cb13d6e1f1586ce. This file is an allocation and audit contract, not a theorem claim.

## Importance

A promoted scientific result must do at least one of the following under an explicit contract:

1. Settle a precisely named open question in a primary source, or give an exact counterexample to a claimed theorem.
2. Extend a serious theorem across its known load-bearing obstruction, rather than merely apply it to a subclass that already satisfies its premises.
3. Improve a sharp exponent, threshold, constant, or unavoidable information/computation cost in a regime where the old bound materially prevented a scientific use. State that use; a smaller sufficient bound alone does not establish practical feasibility.
4. Establish a new reusable mechanism with a proved capability or obstruction, including its full acquisition/execution contract and strongest equally informed comparator.

For allocation, a substantial difficult frontier advance outranks an easy standard corollary. Importance is separate from proof availability, confidence, execution convenience and the number of reports. No invented numerical probabilities or aggregate scores will be used.

## Novelty

Specify the nearest primary theorem and the exact delta. Open its theorem/proof and search the load-bearing mechanism, not only the candidate title. Corpus novelty is weaker than historical novelty. An internally reconstructed result can be useful while priority remains UNKNOWN. A printed theorem whose citations do not establish its scope is a source discrepancy; neither its truth nor falsity follows from that discrepancy.

## Attackability during this run

Name the first unresolved mathematical obligation and a falsifier. Prefer attacks that can change the frontier decision: a complete proof under the original contract, a source-legal counterexample, or a decisive obstruction to a proposed mechanism. A task is poorly attackable if it requires an unavailable proof, an unmaterialized graph with unproved uniform constants, a free spectral/oracle premise, or an unspecified interface. Do not improve attackability by silently strengthening assumptions or dropping costs.

# Algebra first bounded report — 2026-10-08

**Status: reconstructed conditional consequences; original candidate UNKNOWN.** Source handling is `source=DATA`. No formal replay, independent expert review, or external certification was obtained. The repository was read at commit `687dfc0640ee80654bcbdbe38cb13d6e1f1586ce` and was not edited.

The source triage did not produce an exact contradiction to the corrected positive-characteristic or entropy premises. The most useful attack was therefore a line-by-line reconstruction of the family252 incidence geometry. I found no failing premise in that reconstruction. It yields a precise geometric consequence, followed by a published embedding transfer that preserves the entire candidate group. Neither settles the original nonsoficity claim.

## 1. Exact geometric consequence of the incidence construction

Assume the family252 complex is constructed as specified in `construction.tex`, including the incidence girth and block hypotheses, and its CAT(-1) link bounds have been established. For label i, let Θ_i be the two-vertex graph consisting of V,W and the r² parallel edges x_(i,u,v). Then:

* H_i=π₁Θ_i embeds as a quasiconvex free subgroup of G=π₁K, of rank r²−1.
* The subgroups H_i form a malnormal family.
* Each nondegenerate four-edge rectangle is a primitive element of H_i.
* For each edge e of Θ_i the parity homomorphism θ_e:H_i→C₂ gives an explicit index-two quasiconvex free subgroup J_e of rank 2r²−3.
* If a rectangle w is nontrivial in G and is killed by every map from G to a finite group, the four J_e corresponding to its four edges are not separable in G. If the strengthened nonsofic rank conclusion holds, the same w is killed by every map to any sofic group.

This is more precise than the inherited statement that G is not residually finite: the obstruction lies in a primitive element of a specific malnormal quasiconvex free subgroup, and yields explicit finite-index free subgroups with failed separability. It is **conditional on the source construction and residual obstruction**. No incidence table, concrete prime, selected rectangle, or complete presentation was materialized. The statement is not an unconditional construction of a new nonsofic group. Priority for this particular extracted consequence is UNKNOWN; the local-convexity and malnormality mechanisms are classical.
